newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX SIGN STARTER NAVARRO AWAY FROM CUBS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX SIGN STARTER NAVARRO AWAY FROM CUBS.

text.p: Two days after losing ace starter Alex Fernandez, the Chicago White Sox plucked free agent pitcher Jaime Navarro from the crosstown Chicago Cubs.
Navarro, signed to a four-year contract, told WMVP Radio in Chicago that the deal was worth $20 million.
The White Sox also re-signed left-handed reliever Tony Castillo to a two-year contract with a one-year club option.
The 28-year-old Navarro was 15-12 with a 3.92 ERA in 35 starts for the Cubs last season. He led the Cubs in wins, starts, complete games (four), innings (236.2) and strikeouts (158).
"Jaime Navarro gives our rotation an established major league starter who can be counted on to provide us with quality innings," said White Sox official Ron Schueler.
Navarro will be counted on to replace Fernandez, who won 16 games last season, in a rotation that features Wilson Alvarez and James Baldwin.
"I'm looking forward to having Frank Thomas, Albert Belle and Robin Ventura driving in a lot of runs for me," Navarro told WMVP.
Navarro, who won a career-high 17 games with Milwaukee in 1992, has posted 10 or more victories five times in his career and has topped the 200-innings mark five times.
In his two seasons with the Cubs, Navarro went 29-18 with a 3.62 ERA. He is 91-77 lifetime with a 4.10 ERA in eight major league seasons with Milwaukee and the Cubs.

The 33-year-old Castillo split the 1996 season between the Toronto Blue Jays and the White Sox, going 3-1 with one save and a 1.59 ERA in 15 games with the Sox after being acquired on August 22. He was 5-4 with two saves and a 3.60 ERA in 55 games combined last season.
